what_it_does: GPS and navigation receivers must separate incoming signals into two perpendicular components (I and Q channels) to decode the satellite's message. Traditional designs switch between the signal and a reference oscillator to extract these channels, but parasitic capacitances in the switch create phase and amplitude mismatches that degrade positioning accuracy. This paper presents an alternative using transconductor circuits (devices that convert voltage to current in a linear way) to generate the orthogonal channels directly from the RF signal without switches. The result: improved I/Q phase and amplitude balance that's easier to calibrate and more robust, enabling power-efficient, ultra-low-voltage GPS receivers.
